**1. Cross-region hypothesis — refuted by AWS documentation.**
AWS documentation explicitly confirms this is a **supported, documented configuration**:
> *"Amazon Q Business supports cross-region IAM Identity Center and Amazon Q Business integrations only for organization level instances... If you create a cross-region integration... you may experience higher latency... We don't recommend using this feature if you have more than 100 groups per user."* ([Configuring an IAM Identity Center instance for Q Business](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/idc-setup.html))

So an **org-level** Identity Center instance in us-west-2 paired with a Q Business app in us-east-1 is a sanctioned architecture — Q Business makes cross-region calls to fetch user/group attributes. The only documented caveats are added latency and a >100-groups-per-user caution, not a functional block. **If the IC instance were account-level (not org-level), that would be unsupported** — so the instance type (org vs. account) is worth double-checking, but region alone is not the root cause.

**2. Could not trace the actual authorization chain — the named resources are not present/visible in the only AWS account tied to this agent space (012345678901_2).**
- `qbusiness:ListApplications` returned **zero applications** in both us-east-1 and us-west-2.
- `sso-admin:ListInstances` returned **zero instances** in both us-east-1 and us-west-2 (no org or account instance visible).
- CloudTrail (90-day lookback) shows **no `CreateApplication`, `ChatSync`, or other Q Business application activity**, and no Identity Center instance-creation events in this account — only the read-only calls this investigation itself just made.
